title: Catalog of Second Chances (CSC) - Digital Database and Corresponding Interfaces for ReUse of Architectural Components (v0.6.3.1)
description:
The Catalog of Second Chances (CSC) is a prototypical digital component database. It catalogs digital representations of uniquely identifiable architectural components for reuse. Furthermore, it provides corresponding interfaces and tools to leverage them via a backend REST-API, a web-frontend as well as a interface for direct interaction within Rhino Grasshopper.

Changes in v0.6.3.1 (2026-10-21)

A hardening release after 0.6.3.0.

Changed

  • Viewer: mesh edges stay crisp over the faces instead of breaking up at some angles; close zooms no longer cut a piece open, and small pieces open filling the view. A version switch while the mesh or the point cloud is Off loads nothing hidden.
  • Evidence: a core record links to its paired rebound record; a piece with several reinforcement layouts shows all of them.
  • Geometry: replacing the meshes or clouds of a draft also removes the files and markers of the dropped ones; a frame-only cache entry no longer carries descriptor data; the outline vertex limit counts holes.
  • Release tooling: invoke release-prep sets the CHANGELOG date, writes .zenodo.json and runs the version checks in one step; bump-version --gh leaves the Session component alone when its client version already matches. The local launch entries and the old scripts work without a user path; the local server script is now scripts/dev/serve_dump.py (invoke dev-local; invoke dev-migrated still works and says so), migrating an old 0.5 dump only with --migrate; it writes .dev/dev-local-credentials-<port>.txt and .dev/local-<port>.json.

Security

  • Failed access-token lookups are limited per address (429 with Retry-After); valid tokens are never counted.
  • Token clean-up: the tokens and connections of a deleted account are removed with it; revoked and expired tokens are deleted 90 days later.

Server notes

  • Existing token rows get their clean-up date from the daily user maintenance run (not while the read-only flag is set); no step needed.

Full history: CHANGELOG.md
